title: Functions: default arguments, named arguments and single-expression bodies

videos.script: A study session has a course, a length, a date, and whether it is done. In Java, a method that takes all four needs a version for every combination a caller might leave out. {{declare}} Kotlin starts the same way. A name, typed parameters, a return type, and a compiler that checks every way out of the body. {{expr}} Then it gets shorter. A function that is one expression drops its braces, and if stops being a statement and becomes a value. {{named}} Then the part that replaces the overloads. Defaults on the parameters, and names at the call, so true stops being a mystery. {{vararg}} A function that takes any number of values, and the star that unpacks an array into it. {{local}} Functions inside functions, and private ones a file keeps to itself. {{nothing}} And two return types with no value in them. Unit, which means finished. And Nothing, which means never finishes, and which explains the elvis operator from lesson 2.
